messages.subject: Transect effort / blank observations
parts:
Hi all,

I have what I think is a fairly straightforward question. 

I understand for line transect surveys with repeat visits that the effort should reflect the number of visits - so a transect of length 0.3km visited twice would have an effort of 0.6km, for example? I'm just wondering if you then have a visit where no bird was seen, should you still include an observation row with the same accumulated effort and transect details, but with blank species and distance columns ?

Thanks,
Colin

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Transect effort / blank observations
parts:
Exactly right on all points, Colin.

A 0.3km transect visited twice, with no detections on either visit would have effort of 0.6 and NA for perpendicular distance and any other fields at the level of observation.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Transect effort / blank observations
parts:
Colin

That depends whether you are recording "visit" in your data frame. If so, then you would have two rows for a given transect; for the first visit, you would have the detection distance, for the second visit the detection distance would be NA.

Otherwise, if you are pooling the data for the two visits, you would probably not have "visit" in your data.
